sources.weight: Her two bundles are 288 reeds, 144 each, and her ties, lashings and ends eight ropes of six reeds: at the rush mat's calibration, a game reed is about 0.15 kg of dry reed (a 1 m² mat of 8 reeds weighs 1 to 1.5 kg as real rushes), 43.2 kg of bundles and 7.2 kg of cord, as a real 1 cm cord weighs 90 g a metre. A caballito de totora 2.44 × 0.41 × 0.23 m weighs 41 kg dry (festival.si.edu, storied objects, reed raft); hers, 3 × 0.4 × 0.2 m of the same build, 42.8 kg
sources.parts: Reed bundles and reed cord, by weight; the cord counts as flax rope
sources.depthMetres: Her bundles stand 20 cm from bottom to top
sources.shell: Bundles of stems, which a blow bends and an edge parts without harm; she comes apart where an edge cuts a lashing. Reed rope, as flax rope, 1 cm thick; by the model, eight ties 0.5 voxel wide along each bundle's 48 voxels and the five lashings across her cover about a tenth of her sides and a twentieth of her bottom. A breaker's pressure bends the stems, which spring back
sources.soak: Balance on history, per kilogram of reed as the old 60 kg boat took it: the reed takes up a third of its weight in water every six hours afloat, near the 41 kg caballito's 27 kg taken up on a day's fishing (festival.si.edu), and saturates at five times its weight; a sunny day ashore drives four times its weight out again, but each drying leaves a third of what it drove out as rot, so a boat soaked through and dried five times is past saving where Titicaca's totora boats last months

sources.time: A held action lasts the real time of that one piece of work over sixty: game time runs 30 times faster than real time, and boat work is halved again
sources.lashing: One rope is ten metres of cord, some ten turns pulled tight around both bundles: about a quarter of an hour. Her five lashings of two turns, each with its knot, take 11.8 m, two ropes, counted by her shape's builder; the first binds the bundles into her where they lie
sources.tips: Each end is pulled together and up, and bound in a spiral of turns some six centimetres apart, 8.8 m of cord: one rope an end, a quarter of an hour

sources.ends: Her ends stand up only by the stiffness of their bound reed, against their weight; soaked, the reed is heavier and limp, and the ends sag until, saturated, they lie on the water. No line holds them up, as none held Ra I's stern

sources.beamMetres: Her two 20 cm bundles side by side
sources.windageSquareMetres: Her 3 m length over a freeboard of about 5 cm with her rider aboard, and her two raised ends
sources.heave: Reed is light and rises with the crest
sources.capsizeBreakerMetres: Huanchaco's caballitos are paddled out through the surf and ride its breakers in (festival.si.edu): the low float slips under a breaker, which rolls her only once it stands as high as her rider sits, about 0.9 m
sources.rollResponse: Bundles bound into a flat-bottomed hull: a little livelier than vanilla's boats
sources.pitchResponse: Light and short, it lifts to each swell
